text: Okay, I think everyone's here. So today is mostly a brainstorm, no pressure to decide anything. Three things on my list: onboarding, the offsite, and the release notes mess.
Sounds good. Let's start with onboarding, that's the one bugging me.
Right. So the drop-off after signup is still bad. Something like sixty percent never create a second project.
One idea I had is an interactive checklist in the sidebar. Create a project, invite a teammate, connect a repo. You tick them off as you go.
I like that. What about a video walkthrough instead? Like a two minute tour on first login.
We tried videos at my last job. The problem is they go stale every time the UI changes, and nobody re-records them.
Yeah, that's fair. Maintenance cost is real. Let's park the video idea, at least until the UI settles down.
Another angle: a sandbox workspace that's pre-filled with sample data, so people can poke around without setting anything up.
Ooh. That might actually beat the checklist for people who just want to look. Though seeding realistic sample data is its own project.
This is half-baked, but what if we paired new teams with a buddy from the community forum? Like an experienced user who checks in after a week.
Interesting. I don't know how we'd recruit buddies, or what's in it for them. Maybe swag, maybe early access. Worth thinking about.
Let's not decide. Checklist feels cheapest to try though.
Agreed, I'd be happy to mock up the checklist this week so we have something to look at.
Great. Okay, offsite. We said spring. I threw Lisbon out there last time.
Lisbon is lovely, but half the team is in Canada and flights in April are expensive.
Someone suggested a cabin in Vermont. Cheap, driveable for most of us.
The Vermont cabin is cheaper for the Canadian folks but it's a long haul for the two people in Berlin. So it just flips who pays the travel cost.
True. What if we skip travel entirely and do a fully remote hackathon week instead? Ship weird stuff, demo on Friday.
I kind of love that, but people specifically asked for in-person time. A remote hackathon doesn't really replace that.
Maybe both. Hackathon in spring, in-person in the fall when flights are cheaper. Let's not lock it now, I'll need to check budget first.
Do we know the budget at all?
Not yet. Finance said they'd tell us by end of month.
Last one: release notes. Right now it's whoever remembers, writing them the night before.
Could we auto-generate them from commit messages?
We tried that in the old repo. Our commit messages are like 'fix stuff' and 'wip'. The output was useless.
Fair, so that's out unless we enforce conventional commits, and nobody wants that fight right now.
What about having each PR include a one-line user-facing note in the template, and then we just collect them?
That's better. Low effort per PR. The risk is people leave it blank.
We could have a bot nag on PRs without it. Or even have a language model draft the note from the diff and the author just edits it.
The model draft is neat but I'd want to see how often it's wrong before we trust it. The PR template line is the safe first step.
Okay. So nothing decided on the bot, but I'll add the release-note line to the PR template, since that's basically free.
Works for me. Open question for me is who actually owns publishing the notes each release.
Yeah, good question, we'll need to figure that out. Okay, that's time. Thanks everyone.
